items.title: Apple has made a secret AI acquisition – could this mean generative AI is coming to Logic Pro?
items.excerpt: Apple acquired AI audio company Samplab in June, per details disclosed to the European Commission under the DMA — raising the prospect of generative AI audio-editing tools arriving in Logic Pro.

items.title: Just 4 Noise launches ethically-trained AI kick-drum generator
items.excerpt: Just 4 Noise's Just 4 Kicks is an AI kick-drum sample generator trained on licensed material, part of a wider trend of ethically-trained AI tools for producers.

items.title: New studies explore AI expectations, jobs impact and gender gap
items.excerpt: Several recent studies look beyond AI-music debates at how AI will affect jobs, expectations and the gender gap in AI adoption across the creative and wider workforce.

items.title: Session Loops releases PitchNet, a free AI vocal pitch editor
items.excerpt: PitchNet is a free Melodyne-style vocal pitch editor for macOS, Windows and Linux that shows notes in a piano roll and uses AI resynthesis to rebuild the vocal at the edited pitch for smoother, more natural results.

items.title: Is The Humanity of Instruments Under Threat from AI?
items.excerpt: The surge in vibe-coded instrument plugins has been overwhelming, but do we risk losing the most important feature of instruments: humanity?

items.title: Believe, TuneCore Artists Can Opt Into Spotify's AI Remix Tool
items.excerpt: A new licensing agreement lets participating Believe and TuneCore artists opt in to earn royalties from AI-powered fan remixes and covers on Spotify.

items.title: ICMP says AI firms are trying to 'strong-arm' Australia on copyright – and that Kylie Minogue's songs have already been used to train AI
items.excerpt: According to the ICMP, Australia is the only nation seriously considering AI-driven copyright rollbacks; the body says hits by Kylie Minogue and Nick Cave have already been used to train AI without compensation.

items.title: Spotify is dancing around its AI 'slop and spam' problem
items.excerpt: Spotify said it removed 50 million 'slop and spam' tracks from recommendations this year, but hasn't necessarily wiped them from the platform entirely.

items.title: Spotify pulled 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from its recommendations
items.excerpt: Spotify says it has pulled more than 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from its recommendations this year — but it still isn't labeling AI tracks.

items.title: 'Human Made, Human Paid': The Largest U.S. Musicians Union Is Demanding AI Protections
items.excerpt: The AFM's 'Human Made, Human Paid' campaign asks major labels to give musicians a contract with AI protections and compensation.

items.title: Romain Gavras Is Bummed About Those AI Versions of "Storm"
items.excerpt: The director reacts to AI-generated knockoffs of his 'Storm' video: 'Part of me wanted to quit filmmaking, move back to Greece, and become an olive farmer.'

items.title: MIRA: A Musical Intent Refinement Agent for Aligning Text-to-Music Generation with User Intent
items.excerpt: An agent that refines user musical intent for text-to-music systems, arguing global text-audio relevance scores overlook implicit intent and proposing finer-grained alignment.
